text: The Patriots orchestrated one of Week 4's most significant comebacks, engineering a 29-26 upset victory over the Bills at Buffalo's new Highmark Stadium—a result that carried particular weight for the defending AFC champions, as Mike Vrabel emphasized in his Monday press conference. Drake Maye, who had struggled through the early season, delivered when it mattered most, mounting a clutch game-winning drive despite coughing up two turnovers; his three touchdown passes proved sufficient to overcome those miscues and hand Josh Allen his first defeat of the season. The offense broke out in explosive fashion against a Bills defense that couldn't contain the Patriots' attack, and the victory marked a dramatic inflection point for New England, pulling them to 2-2 alongside the Rams and Cowboys as this trio of teams simultaneously staged stunning rallies to save what looked like doomed seasons. Whether this comeback signals the Patriots are truly back on track for another AFC East title, as some suggested afterward, remains to be judged—though stopping overreactions to one Week 4 win is always wise in October.
